question: is the iid benchmark operating point p=0.05 derivable from the calibrated channel as a per-encoder-pass physical error probability (the old ~1%-per-gate argument), or is it a convention?

calibrated_channel.note: all three roles (control f_k=k / target f=1,2,3 / spectator f_k=k) give identically 3.459e-2 at q=3 -- the |Delta f| multiset is the same; active-block depolarization would ADD to the active roles; whole-register per-gate-step p_phys=0.376 (paper Sec III) is the register-level anchor

old_argument_reconstruction: a ~1%-per-gate reading requires eta~0.980 (sigma_p2~0.020), i.e. ~3.5x below the calibrated variance; at the calibrated point the per-gate per-qudit dephasing infidelity is 3.46e-2
verdict: NOT DERIVABLE as a per-encoder-pass quantity: even the minimal L=2 a2a encoder (40 MS gates, every gate dephasing every qudit) accumulates per-qudit error probability ~0.76 per pass at the calibrated point -- 15x above p=0.05. p=0.05 instead sits at ~1.4x the SINGLE-GATE per-qudit infidelity (3.46e-2). RECOMMENDED REFRAMING: p=0.05 is a stated convention approximating one-to-two entangling-gate steps of calibrated per-qudit noise, NOT an encoder-pass equivalent; any per-pass reading would put every code in the >0.15 regime where the ranking inverts (Table I).
